rounds.proof_sketch: The removed __syncthreads() guards a WAR hazard on shared_mem[0]. For race to occur, thread 0 must complete 256+ loop iterations before other warps read shared_mem[0]. After prior sync, all warps start together, and a single read instruction completes far before any warp finishes its loop. Loop iteration count is fixed (feature_size/blockDim.x), not data-dependent.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation creates a theoretical data race between reading shared_mem[0] (to compute mean) and writing shared_mem[tid] (thread 0 writes to shared_mem[0]). However, this race is not triggerable through value manipulation because the execution path has no data-dependent control flow. The var_sum loop executes a fixed number of iterations regardless of input values. After the preceding __syncthreads(), all warps are synchronized and execute the read instruction together before any warp could possibly complete the hundreds of loop iterations needed to reach the write. The race window is timing-based, not value-based, making it unkillable under the fixed-shape, variable-value contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable through value manipulation. The race condition depends on thread scheduling timing, which cannot be influenced by input tensor values. The mutation represents undefined behavior that happens to be practically equivalent on current CUDA implementations for this kernel structure.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of synchronization barriers, consider hardware-level stress testing (varying GPU load, frequency scaling) or formal verification tools rather than value-level differential testing. Sync-removal mutations often create Heisenbugs that are correct 99.99% of the time but represent latent bugs.
